summary: This YAML file defines a Docker service called 'docs' that builds an image from the current directory, mounts the local workspace inside the container, exposes port 4242, sets up a Python path to find scripts, and runs a startup command that makes a script executable then keeps the container running indefinitely.

explanations.3: The 'build: .' tells Docker to create an image using the Dockerfile in the current directory.
explanations.5: This mounts the current directory (.) on your computer to /workspace inside the container, so changes you make locally show up immediately in the container.
explanations.7: The '%%port=4242%%' syntax appears to be a placeholder that gets replaced with an actual port number at runtime; the ':4242' maps that port inside the container to the same port on your computer.
explanations.9: This tells Python where to look for importable modules — in this case, the /workspace/scripts folder.
explanations.10: The '>' character means the command continues on the next line(s) as a single multi-line string.
explanations.11: The script makes preview.sh executable with chmod, then 'sleep infinity' keeps the container running indefinitely so you can interact with it.
